headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: gpt-researcher can read files and call external APIs while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a docs-only content source with no runtime isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read files and use MCP/API-driven workflows, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so injection risk is limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies B-generated text into A-facing prompts or docs workflows, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared MCP or file bridge, attacker-controlled content can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Keep A as read-only reference material.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace bridge.
Require manual review before reusing B output in prompts.
Use separate sessions for A and B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags on any shared content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets and local documents and can send content to external APIs; A is a docs-only repository, so it is not itself a data sink. The pairwise leakage path is B exposing sensitive inputs or outputs to third parties, with A providing no containment. This is plausible in default research workflows, though not proven for A.
conditions: IF B processes local documents containing sensitive data, those contents may be transmitted to external APIs.
IF A-derived guidance is pasted into B workflows that include secrets, the combined workflow can leak those secrets through B.
mitigations: Avoid feeding secrets into B tasks.
Use redacted sample documents for research runs.
Restrict B API keys to least privilege.
Separate A reference browsing from B document processing.
requires-engineering: route sensitive workloads to a local-only backend.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or runtime capabilities, while B can read files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. There is no shared writable resource or locking model documented between them, so direct capability conflict is weak. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator to place both on the same mutable workspace.
conditions: IF an orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF B is extended with write privileges not shown in its profile, overlap risk increases.
mitigations: Run A and B in separate directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Serialize B jobs that touch shared artifacts.
Use read-only mounts for A.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B has a planner/execution/publisher pattern and can act on research outputs, while A is a prompt-engineering content source that may be treated as authoritative guidance. Because A has no verification or runtime controls, B can propagate A-derived instructions or facts without a built-in check. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses A’s content as authoritative research guidance without verification, errors can cascade into published outputs.
IF B’s publisher step consumes A-derived claims, downstream actions may reflect unverified content.
mitigations: Require source verification before publication.
Mark A content as non-authoritative reference only.
Add a human review step before B publishes.
Cross-check claims against primary sources.
requires-engineering: enforce citation validation in the publisher.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public open-source docs repository with no touched data classes, while B processes local documents and external research data under multiple API integrations. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance concern exists if sensitive documents are routed through B. A is not a direct compliance sink here.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent through B’s external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF A is used to curate policy text for B without review, compliance guidance may be outdated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B runs.
Use non-sensitive test corpora.
Review API retention settings.
Document data-handling boundaries.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing.
